candidates.title: Gemini 4 Argon makes million-token output a production choice, not a demo
candidates.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Argon as a stable paid API model with a unified 1,048,576-token input-output budget, optional million-token long decode, multiple consumption tiers, and a mixed vendor-reported coding benchmark profile.
candidates.what_changed: The stable `gemini-4-argon` endpoint is generally available with multimodal input, 65,536-token default synchronous output, optional long decode up to the unified 1,048,576-token limit, and documented Standard, Batch, Flex, and Priority pricing.
candidates.why_it_matters: Repository-scale and long-running agents can produce much larger artifacts in one interaction, but the same envelope raises latency, cost, validation, and blast-radius requirements; benchmark results also vary enough that harness-specific evaluation remains necessary.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Treat long decode as a separate workload class with token and spend ceilings, checkpoints, acceptance tests, and hard tool boundaries; benchmark the exact repository and harness rather than selecting from one aggregate coding claim.

evidence.rationale: Google's release notes and model reference establish GA availability, endpoint, limits, capabilities, and pricing; Google DeepMind's model card provides the benchmark table, limitations, and frontier-risk assessment.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent reproduction of Argon's long-decode behavior, benchmark table, latency, or safety mitigations was found during this run.
evidence.claim_scope: The story distinguishes official product facts from vendor-reported evaluations and does not claim overall coding-model leadership.

signal.rationale: A stable frontier reasoning model with an optional million-token decode path materially changes the design and cost envelope for autonomous engineering workflows.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: Pulse has covered context windows and reasoning settings, but not the operational distinction between a unified token budget, default output limit, and opt-in long-decode workflow.
learning_gap.suggested_explainer: Long Decode Is Not Just a Larger Context Window

follow_up_opportunities.reason: The release exposes a reusable distinction among input context, unified token budgets, output caps, long decode, caching, and runtime spend.

deduplication.canonical_event: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon as a stable generally available API model on October 13, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: No merged Pulse story or ledger covers Gemini 4 Argon, its GA endpoint, long-decode limits, prices, evaluations, or safety case.

publication_verification.notes: The dated Gemini API release note, current model reference, pricing page, and DeepMind model card were rechecked. Benchmark and safety results remain vendor-reported and are labeled accordingly.

candidates.title: Google's overnight ADK run shows why coding-agent output still needs subtraction
candidates.summary: Google Cloud published the prompts, repository skills, full-test behavior, rejected changes, merged commit, and holdout benchmark design from an 11-hour unattended performance run on the 205,000-line Python ADK repository.
candidates.what_changed: A first-hand account now documents how `.agents/skills`, a persistent `/goal`, four baseline workloads, the full 16,892-test suite, and a prewritten holdout benchmark turned six agent proposals into two reviewed changes merged across 22 files.
candidates.why_it_matters: The account provides rare operational evidence about both the successful changes and the four rejected optimizations, showing that repository instructions and long runtime help only when independent measurement and maintainer subtraction remain in the loop.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Give unattended agents outcome-level goals and discoverable repository rules, require one unmerged review artifact, predefine baseline and holdout checks, run the complete suite, and audit discarded ideas as carefully as the final diff.

evidence.rationale: The named engineers publish the prompt, instruction structure, run chronology, test counts, accepted and rejected changes, benchmark method, and scoped results; the merged public commit exposes the shipped diff and benchmark note.
evidence.independent_validation: The public commit validates the landed code and recorded measurements, but the private overnight session log and comparison of runs were not independently observed.
evidence.claim_scope: The story presents a first-hand case study and reusable workflow, not a general success-rate claim for Argon or unattended coding agents.

signal.rationale: The post provides unusually detailed evidence about how a serious engineering organization configured, evaluated, and reviewed a long-running coding agent on a mature repository.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: The story can teach the workflow directly without a prerequisite Foundation explainer.

follow_up_opportunities.reason: The published prompt, skill layout, benchmark sequence, CI gate, pull-request boundary, and review findings support a concrete reusable operating checklist.

deduplication.canonical_event: Google Cloud publishes an inspectable 11-hour coding-agent case study and merged ADK optimization on October 13, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: No prior Pulse story covers this ADK run, its repository-skill configuration, rejected proposals, holdout method, or merged commit.

publication_verification.notes: The dated engineering post and merged commit were rechecked. The story scopes the performance figures to the documented workloads and identifies which run evidence remains first-party.

candidates.title: ML Drift replaces TFLite's GPU delegate path with one cross-platform inference core
candidates.summary: Google open-sourced ML Drift, LiteRT's cross-platform GPU engine, while ending new feature work on the legacy TFLite GPU delegate and documenting deployments across Google products and external partners.
candidates.what_changed: The Apache-2.0 runtime is now available as both LiteRT's GPU accelerator and a standalone library, with tensor virtualization across OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU, custom-op APIs, 5D tensors, stage-aware LLM kernels, and a repository skill for custom shaders.
candidates.why_it_matters: Teams deploying on-device AI now have an inspectable forward path for LiteRT GPU acceleration backed by broad production use, but migration still depends on backend, packaging, operator, device, memory, and thermal validation.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Build a device-and-backend compatibility matrix, benchmark end-to-end latency and peak memory on representative hardware, validate custom ops against fallbacks, and treat the legacy delegate's feature freeze as a roadmap signal.

evidence.rationale: Google's technical release describes the architecture, migration direction, deployment footprint, configurations, and benchmark claims; the Apache-2.0 repository and LiteRT documentation expose the implementation and integration path.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent cross-device benchmark of ML Drift or verification of partner deployment results was found during this run.
evidence.claim_scope: The story reports vendor performance figures as scoped examples and does not infer a universal speedup or compatibility guarantee.

signal.rationale: The open-source release and feature freeze on the legacy delegate establish a durable platform transition for on-device AI inference.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: Pulse has not published a reusable guide to the split between prefill and decode or to validating portable GPU inference across heterogeneous devices.
learning_gap.suggested_explainer: Prefill, Decode, and Memory Traffic on Edge GPUs

follow_up_opportunities.reason: The open repository supports a separate implementation review of tensor virtualization, backend lowering, stage-aware kernels, operator fallback, and the production benchmark configurations.

deduplication.canonical_event: Google open-sources ML Drift and makes it the forward LiteRT GPU path on October 8, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: The merged archive through October 13 contains no ML Drift story, candidate, source URL, or event record.

publication_verification.notes: The October 8 technical post, current source repository, and LiteRT documentation were rechecked. Deployment and performance claims remain first-party and are scoped in the story.

candidates.title: Copilot can now refuse startup when enterprise policy is stale
candidates.summary: GitHub added a managed setting that can force supported Copilot clients to confirm current remote policy at startup and fail closed when they cannot, plus minimum client-version enforcement for the managed sandbox key.
candidates.what_changed: Administrators can set `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh=true` through server, MDM, or file delivery; a cached response no longer satisfies freshness, and older clients pinned below the sandbox policy's required version must update before Copilot resumes.
candidates.why_it_matters: Enterprise agent governance can now make policy freshness and client capability prerequisites for execution instead of assuming a cached control plane is current, at the cost of a deliberate availability dependency.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Choose the failure mode explicitly, use device or file management for first-sign-in enforcement, test offline and service-outage startup, inventory pinned versions, and canary the sandbox minimum before broad rollout.

evidence.rationale: GitHub's dated changelog defines the setting name, supported clients, delivery paths, cache behavior, first-sign-in distinction, fail-closed outcome, and sandbox minimum-version enforcement.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent cross-client test of startup failure or version enforcement was found.
evidence.claim_scope: The story reports the documented management contract and operational trade-off without claiming identical implementation on every client.

signal.rationale: The update changes the failure mode of enterprise coding-agent governance from cached resilience to optionally mandatory policy freshness.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: Recent Pulse coverage of Copilot managed telemetry and MXC-backed sandboxing provides enough context for the material update.

deduplication.canonical_event: GitHub adds fail-closed managed-policy refresh and sandbox client-version enforcement on October 13, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: The October 8 story covered the local sandbox boundary and the October 13 story covered telemetry capture policy. This release adds startup-time policy freshness, distinct bootstrap behavior by delivery channel, failure on unconfirmed policy, and a minimum-version gate for the sandbox setting.

publication_verification.notes: The dated GitHub changelog and current deployment documentation were rechecked. Enforcement behavior remains first-party documentation and is not presented as independently tested.

watchlist.title: Gemini 4 Argon extends one model into robotics workflows
watchlist.summary: Google describes Argon workflows spanning multi-view video, geometry, simulation, code generation, and robot control, but the publication is a launch demonstration rather than independent embodied evaluation.

evidence.rationale: Google provides official workflow descriptions and access paths, but no independent replication or standardized physical-task comparison accompanies the launch post.

signal.rationale: A general frontier model crossing simulation and physical control could be consequential, but the current evidence does not establish reliability or transfer beyond curated workflows.

watchlist.reason: The article is a vendor launch narrative tied to the already selected Argon release and lacks independent physical-task validation, failure analysis, or reproducible end-to-end results.
promote_when: Independent benchmark or real-robot replication with task definitions and failure rates.
A reproducible implementation documents the perception-to-control loop, safety boundary, and simulation-to-real transfer.

watchlist.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 unifies local multimodal retrieval in a modular sub-1B model
watchlist.summary: Google released an Apache-2.0 embedding model with modular text, vision, and audio encoders that map into one 768-dimensional space and can be truncated for smaller vector stores.

evidence.rationale: Google publishes model sizes, modalities, integration examples, and vendor evaluation claims.

signal.rationale: The model could simplify private multimodal retrieval, but the release predates the current research window and no independent cross-modal retrieval or device benchmark was found.

watchlist.reason: The open model is technically relevant, but selection would rely primarily on delayed vendor claims during a stronger batch and without independent retrieval-quality, latency, or memory validation.
promote_when: Independent benchmark across text, code, image, video, and audio retrieval.
A first-hand deployment reports device memory, latency, index size, and quality at truncated dimensions.
